title: National Fire Pup Day: why Dalmatians ended up in firehouses
dek: October 1 is National Fire Pup Day. Here is how Dalmatians became firehouse dogs and what fire department dogs do today.
keyPoints: In the 1700s, Dalmatians ran alongside carriages as guard dogs.
In the 1800s, they moved into firehouses because they kept horses calm.
Today, fire department dogs work in search and rescue, arson detection and community outreach.

body: If you have ever wondered why the classic firehouse dog is a spotted Dalmatian, today is a good day for the answer. October 1 is National Fire Pup Day, which recognizes the dogs that serve with fire departments.

The connection goes back to horses. According to National Today, Dalmatians were used in the 1700s as carriage dogs, running beside coaches to guard travelers and their belongings on dangerous roads. When fire departments began using horse-drawn engines in the 1800s, the dogs came along. They were known for having a calming effect on horses, which helped when the engines raced through busy streets, and their spotted coats were easy to see at night and in smoke.

When engines replaced horses, the job changed. Many fire pups became mascots and community ambassadors, often showing up at school visits and safety events. Others do serious work. Some fire departments use dogs for search and rescue, and some use trained dogs for arson detection, since a dog's nose can pick up traces of substances used to start fires.
These are working animals, and their handlers decide when it is a good time for people to say hello. A working dog that is on duty may need to stay focused.
If you meet a fire department dog at a community event, ask the handler before petting it. That is a good habit with any working dog.
